title.narrative: GCERF - Stärka hållbar återintegrering och lokal motståndskraft 2026-2029
GCERF - Sustainable Reintegration and Community Resilience 2026-2029

description.narrative: Projektet omfattar två landprogram i Irak och Uzbekistan med fokus på hållbart återvändande och återintegrering, minskad sårbarhet för marginalisering, irreguljär migration och våldsbejakande extremism samt stärkt kapacitet hos myndigheter, civilsamhälle och lokalsamhällen att stödja återvändare och förebygga utsatthet och radikalisering.

The project comprises two country programmes in Iraq and Uzbekistan, focusing on sustainable return and reintegration, reducing vulnerability to marginalisation, irregular migration and violent extremism, and strengthening the capacity of authorities and civil society to support returnees. In Iraq, this includes rehabilitation, psychosocial and legal support, education and livelihoods, while in Uzbekistan the focus is on preventing irregular migration and human trafficking, strengthening returnee support and economic resilience, and enhancing local actors’ capacity to prevent radicalisation.

The project consists of two country programmes in Iraq and Uzbekistan, with a shared focus on sustainable return, reintegration, and reducing vulnerability to marginalisation, irregular migration, and violent extremism. The interventions also aim to strengthen the capacity of government authorities and civil society to support returnees.
In Iraq, the project focuses on providing returnees with access to rehabilitation, psychosocial and legal support, as well as education and livelihood opportunities. At the same time, local communities capacity to support reintegration is strengthened through local initiatives, dialogue, and activities that promote social cohesion. Young people and women are given a particular role in prevention efforts and in strengthening trust and a sense of community.
In Uzbekistan, the focus is on preventing irregular migration and human trafficking, while strengthening support for returnees. This includes psychosocial and legal support, education, vocational training, and livelihood opportunities. The project also strengthens economic resilience through, for example, financial literacy training, micro-grants, and support for entrepreneurship. Local authorities and civil society actors are simultaneously provided with increased capacity to identify and prevent radicalisation.
In summary, the project combines support for returnees with efforts to promote social cohesion, economic resilience, and prevention at the local level.
